dedupe_keys.name: pub drain water level sensors and flood alerts api singapore data gov sg

description: PUB, Singapore's national water agency, publishes on the national open data portal the locations of its drain and canal water level sensors and a real-time API of flood alert events across the island. The sensor layer, created in 2023 and last updated on 13 April 2026 on a half-yearly cycle, lists each sensor point with a name and description in a small XLSX or GeoJSON file, while the flood alerts API returns timestamped observation records every few minutes; PUB notes that flood warning notices are not included. PUB states that its Catchment and Waterways Operations System integrates more than 1,000 water level sensors, over 500 CCTV cameras, rain gauges, weather radar and response vehicle locations, and live levels can be viewed in its water level viewer. Both sets are free under the Singapore Open Data Licence, which allows commercial use. Caveats: the portal gives sensor locations but not the historical water level series, alert records can be empty when no flooding occurs, and the page layer size suggests it may cover fewer sensors than PUB's total. Simulation uses: real-time and event data for urban flash flood models and digital twins of the drainage system, validating drainage capacity under intense rainfall, emergency response routing, and climate adaptation of canals and drains. Related records: the Dutch LIWO maps (data-netherlands-liwo-flood-information) are a scenario-based counterpart for national flood information.
